summary: Integrate PentestAgent (https://github.com/GH05TCREW/pentestagent) — an AI agent framework for black-box security testing — into the Namias portfolio to achieve top-tier security posture. Deliverables include automated reconnaissance playbooks, vulnerability scanning, API security testing, CI/CD security gates, remediation of all findings, and a comprehensive security dashboard showcasing the portfolio as a capstone security project.
narrative: The Namias portfolio is a Next.js App Router marketing site with 50+ components, 6 API routes (chat, resume, media, sanity webhook, sanity live, draft-mode), Sanity CMS integration, Cal.com booking embeds, and Umami analytics. With this growing surface area, a proactive security posture is essential — not just defensive hardening (rate limiting, input sanitisation, env hygiene) but continuous automated black-box testing via PentestAgent. PentestAgent is a Python-based AI agent framework that orchestrates LLM-driven security agents for reconnaissance, vulnerability scanning, exploitation, and reporting. This slice installs PentestAgent, creates the configuration, writes custom playbooks for the portfolio's attack surface, runs the scans, remediates every finding, and integrates the results into CI/CD and a security dashboard. The deliverable is a reference-grade security programme that hiring managers can inspect as proof of the owner's security engineering skills.
principles: Defence in depth — PentestAgent complements existing rate-limiting, input sanitisation, and env hygiene from the Security-Hardening branch.
Every finding is a commit — scan results, remediation commits, and re-verification each get their own commit for auditability.
Playbooks are reusable — each PentestAgent playbook targets a specific attack vector and can be re-run on demand.
CI is the enforcement point — automated scans run on every PR and on a schedule; failures block merges.
Document the journey — the security dashboard shows the full posture, not just the final score.
No behaviour change without verification — every remediation is verified by re-running the relevant scan.

personas.label: PP Namias (owner)
goals: Demonstrate top-tier security engineering by making the portfolio itself the capstone project.
Have automated security scans that prove the site is hardened against OWASP Top 10 vectors.
Showcase a security dashboard that hiring managers can inspect.
painPointsToday: No automated security scanning beyond npm audit.
No black-box testing against the live site.
No security dashboard or posture score to show.

personas.label: OpenCode / future coding agent
goals: Read a single SKILL.md and know how to run, read, and fix PentestAgent findings.
Be able to re-run any scan playbook and interpret the results.
Know which findings are fixable and which require architectural changes.
painPointsToday: No baseline scan results to compare against.
No list of acceptable vs blocked playbook patterns.

personas.label: Hiring manager / security reviewer
goals: See a comprehensive security dashboard with scan results, posture score, and fix commit history.
Click into any finding and see the remediation commit.
Trust that the security programme is real (not just documentation).
painPointsToday: No visible security posture signal in the repo.
Hard to distinguish between documented intentions and actual security controls.
No way to verify the site is tested regularly.

primary: Every OWASP Top 10 category is covered by at least one PentestAgent playbook.
All API endpoints pass black-box testing with zero high-severity findings.
A scheduled CI workflow runs PentestAgent scans weekly and posts results as a CI artifact.
A security dashboard exists at docs/security/dashboard.md showing posture score and fix history.
secondary: Each playbook has a documented runbook in docs/security/playbooks/.
All findings are tracked in a findings ledger with status, severity, and fix commit.
The security.txt file is deployed at /.well-known/security.txt.
demo: Local: python pentestagent run -t https://namias.tech --playbook portfolio_recon yields structured findings.
CI: A PR with a deliberate security regression is blocked by the PentestAgent check.
Dashboard: docs/security/dashboard.md shows green/amber/red per category with history.

antiPatterns: Running PentestAgent against production without proper rate-limiting safeguards — scans must respect robots.txt and use reasonable delays.
Committing API keys or secrets in PentestAgent config files — all secrets go in .env.
Silencing findings without fixing them — every legitimate finding must have a corresponding remediation commit.
Touching production data during scans — scans run against the live site but only use GET/HEAD for recon and safe POST payloads for API testing.
PentestAgent findings becoming stale — scans must be re-runnable and results timestamped.

epics.title: Bootstrap PentestAgent infrastructure
epics.summary: Clone PentestAgent repo, set up Python venv, create .env config, create directory structure for custom playbooks and findings, and document the setup. Since the local environment is Python 3.8 (PentestAgent requires 3.10+), the CI pipeline will be the primary execution environment, but all config and playbooks are authored and committed.

stories.title: Create directory structure for PentestAgent integration
stories.details: Create docs/security/pentestagent/ (configs, playbooks, findings, reports), .agents/skills/run-pentestagent/, and a PentestAgent section in the PRD.

stories.title: Create PentestAgent .env.example
stories.details: Create docs/security/pentestagent/.env.example with all required env vars: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, PENTESTAGENT_MODEL, TAVILY_API_KEY, etc. Document which vars are required and which are optional.

stories.title: Create PentestAgent configuration file
stories.details: Create docs/security/pentestagent/config/pentestagent.json with target configuration: target URL (namias.tech), rate limiting delays, allowed tools (terminal, browser, web_search), max concurrent tasks, and output directory.

stories.title: Create PentestAgent MCP server config
stories.details: Create docs/security/pentestagent/config/mcp_servers.json defining any MCP servers to connect (e.g., nmap-mcp for network scanning, MetasploitMCP for exploitation testing). Document in the config.

stories.title: Create setup script for PentestAgent
stories.details: Create scripts/setup-pentestagent.ps1 (Windows) and scripts/setup-pentestagent.sh (Linux/macOS) that clone the repo, create venv, install deps, install Playwright, and copy config files.

stories.title: Document PentestAgent setup in AGENTS.md
stories.details: Add a new skill entry for 'run-pentestagent' in AGENTS.md with a summary, prerequisites, and link to the skill file.

stories.title: Add PentestAgent to .gitignore
stories.details: Ensure pentestagent/ directory is in .gitignore (the cloned tool, not our config) and docs/security/pentestagent/findings/ is also ignored (artifacts).

epics.title: Reconnaissance playbooks & scanning
epics.summary: Create PentestAgent playbooks for reconnaissance: URL enumeration, technology fingerprinting, route discovery, JS endpoint extraction, subdomain discovery, and directory enumeration. Run scans against the live portfolio site and document findings.

stories.title: Create portfolio_recon playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/portfolio_recon.yaml — a PentestAgent playbook that: 1) Enumerates all public routes, 2) Extracts API endpoints from JS bundles, 3) Identifies technology stack (Next.js version, hosting provider, CDN), 4) Maps all third-party connections, 5) Discovers hidden endpoints via common paths. Document the playbook structure.

stories.title: Create technology_fingerprint playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/technology_fingerprint.yaml — identifies: Next.js version, React version, Node version (from headers), hosting provider (Vercel), CDN, analytics tools, CMS (Sanity), font providers, embedded services (Cal.com).

stories.title: Create js_endpoint_extraction playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/js_endpoint_extraction.yaml — downloads all JS chunks from _next/static/, extracts fetch/axios calls, route patterns, and API endpoint URLs. Outputs a structured endpoint map.

stories.title: Create directory_enumeration playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/directory_enumeration.yaml — checks for common paths: /.env, /.git/config, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /api/, /admin/, /_next/, /sw.js, /.well-known/, /security.txt, /health, /favicon.ico, /api/chat, /api/resume, etc.

stories.title: Create subdomain_discovery playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/subdomain_discovery.yaml — discovers subdomains via: DNS enumeration, certificate transparency logs (crt.sh), search engine dorking. Checks for: namias.tech, *.namias.tech, pp-namias.vercel.app.

stories.title: Run recon playbooks and document findings
stories.details: In CI or local environment run the recon playbooks. Document all findings in docs/security/pentestagent/findings/recon.md with screenshots or structured output.

epics.title: Vulnerability scanning playbooks
epics.summary: Create PentestAgent playbooks for OWASP Top 10 vulnerability scanning: XSS, CSRF, SSRF, injection attacks, security misconfiguration, and sensitive data exposure. Run scans, categorise findings, and document results.

stories.title: Create xss_testing playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/xss_testing.yaml — tests for reflected, stored, and DOM-based XSS across all user input points: chat message input, URL query params, search params, form fields. Tests payloads: , , javascript:alert(1), etc.

stories.title: Create csrf_testing playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/csrf_testing.yaml — tests for CSRF protection on all state-changing endpoints: /api/chat, /api/sanity/webhook, /api/draft-mode/enable. Checks for: SameSite cookies, CSRF tokens, Origin/Referer validation.

stories.title: Create ssrf_testing playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/ssrf_testing.yaml — tests for SSRF via: chat endpoint (does it fetch user-provided URLs?), image processing, any proxy-like functionality. Payloads: file:///etc/passwd, http://169.254.169.254/ (metadata), http://localhost:3000/.

stories.title: Create injection_testing playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/injection_testing.yaml — tests for: SQL injection (if any DB), NoSQL injection, Command injection (if any shell exec), Template injection, LDAP injection, Path traversal in /api/media/[...path].

stories.title: Create security_misconfig playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/security_misconfig.yaml — checks for: missing security headers, CORS misconfiguration, open ports, debug endpoints enabled, verbose error messages, stack traces exposed, directory listing enabled, default credentials.

stories.title: Create sensitive_data_exposure playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/sensitive_data_exposure.yaml — checks for: API keys in client-side JS, source maps exposing source code, env vars in HTML responses, PII in responses, credit card or SSN patterns, internal IP addresses, cloud metadata endpoints.

stories.title: Run vulnerability scan playbooks and document findings
stories.details: Run all vulnerability scan playbooks in CI. Document all findings in docs/security/pentestagent/findings/vulnerabilities.md with severity, category, affected endpoint, and evidence.

epics.title: API security testing playbooks
epics.summary: Create PentestAgent playbooks specifically for testing the 6 API endpoints: rate limiting, authentication bypass, input validation, payload limits, CORS configuration, and HTTP method testing. Run scans and document findings.

stories.title: Create rate_limit_testing playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/rate_limit_testing.yaml — tests rate limiting on each endpoint: sends burst requests (50+ in 1s), checks for 429 responses, tests window reset behaviour, tests IP-based vs user-based limiting, tests if rate limiting can be bypassed via X-Forwarded-For spoofing.

stories.title: Create auth_bypass_testing playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/auth_bypass_testing.yaml — tests for auth bypass on protected endpoints: /api/sanity/webhook, /api/sanity/live, /api/draft-mode/enable. Tests: missing secret, wrong secret, empty secret, secret in body vs header vs query, token manipulation, JWT attacks (if applicable).

stories.title: Create input_validation_testing playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/input_validation_testing.yaml — tests input validation across all endpoints: oversized payloads, malformed JSON, unexpected content types, null bytes, Unicode attacks, type confusion, prototype pollution, parameter pollution.

stories.title: Create cors_http_methods playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/cors_http_methods.yaml — tests CORS headers on each endpoint: reflects Origin?, allows null origin?, allows wildcard?, allows credentials from any origin?. Tests HTTP method override: PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS, TRACE on GET-only and POST-only endpoints. Tests OPTIONS preflight behaviour.

stories.title: Create api_fuzz playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/api_fuzz.yaml — fuzzes API endpoints with: boundary values, negative numbers, special characters, format string attacks (%s, %n, %x), long strings (10000+ chars), empty strings, null values, array/object type confusion, duplicate keys.

stories.title: Create dependency_check playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/dependency_check.yaml — runs npm audit, checks for known CVEs in key dependencies: next, react, next-sanity, swr, framer-motion, lucide-react. Compares against national vulnerability database.

stories.title: Run API security playbooks and document findings
stories.details: Run all API security playbooks. Document all findings in docs/security/pentestagent/findings/api-security.md with endpoint, test, result, and severity.

epics.title: Infrastructure & configuration security
epics.summary: Verification of the security infrastructure: HTTP security headers, CSP analysis, cookie security, TLS/SSL configuration, Cloudflare Workers security, Vercel configuration, DNS security, and CDN configuration.

stories.title: Create header_security playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/header_security.yaml — checks every HTTP response header for: CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP, CORP, X-DNS-Prefetch-Control, X-Powered-By, Server header. Verifies values match security best practices.

stories.title: Create csp_analysis playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/csp_analysis.yaml — deep analysis of Content-Security-Policy: checks for unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, wildcard sources (https:, *.), missing directives, eval() usage, blob: usage, data: usage, frame-src for Cal.com, upgrade-insecure-requests effectiveness.

stories.title: Create cookie_security playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/cookie_security.yaml — examines all cookies set by the site: Secure flag, HttpOnly flag, SameSite attribute, Domain/Path scope, Expires/Max-Age. Checks for session cookies, draft-mode cookies, analytics cookies. Verifies localStorage and sessionStorage usage.

stories.title: Create tls_security playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/tls_security.yaml — checks: TLS version (1.2+, 1.3), certificate validity, certificate issuer, HSTS preload status, cipher suites, OCSP stapling, certificate transparency, wildcard vs specific cert, redirect HTTP→HTTPS.

stories.title: Create cloud_config playbook
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/playbooks/cloud_config.yaml — checks Vercel and Cloudflare Workers configuration: Vercel.json for exposed env vars, function timeout, memory allocation. Cloudflare Workers for TOKEN exposure, worker script leaks, route configuration.

stories.title: Run infrastructure playbooks and document findings
stories.details: Run all infrastructure security playbooks. Document findings in docs/security/pentestagent/findings/infrastructure.md.

epics.title: CI/CD security integration
epics.summary: Integrate PentestAgent scans into the CI/CD pipeline: PR checks, scheduled scans, artifact generation, and security dashboard updates. Every scan run produces a timestamped report stored as a CI artifact.

stories.title: Create pentestagent-ci.yml GitHub Action
stories.details: Write .github/workflows/pentestagent-ci.yml — runs on push/PR to security/ branches and main. Steps: checkout, setup Python 3.11, install PentestAgent, run recon playbook, run vulnerability scan playbook, upload findings as CI artifact. Uses secrets for API keys.

stories.title: Create scheduled security scan workflow
stories.details: Write .github/workflows/pentestagent-scheduled.yml — runs weekly (Sunday 02:00 UTC). Runs full playbook suite (recon + vulnerability + API + infrastructure). Compares with previous scan results. Generates diff report. Posts results as CI artifact and optionally creates a GitHub Issue for new findings.

stories.title: Create security-pr-check workflow
stories.details: Write .github/workflows/pentestagent-pr-check.yml — runs on every PR to main. Lightweight scan: checks security headers, checks for known vulnerability patterns in diff, runs dependency audit. Posts security check result as a PR comment. Fails if critical findings detected.

stories.title: Add security-scan to pr-validation.yml
stories.details: Extend .github/workflows/pr-validation.yml to include the new pentestagent-pr-check job in the dependency chain. Update the PR comment template to include security scan results.

stories.title: Document CI/CD security integration
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/reports/ci-integration.md documenting: what each workflow does, how to read scan results, how to re-run scans, what secrets are needed, how to interpret the pass/fail criteria.

epics.title: Remediation of findings
epics.summary: Walk through every finding from EPIC-1 through EPIC-4, remediate each one, and re-verify. Each remediation gets its own commit. Track the status in a findings ledger.

stories.title: Create findings ledger
stories.details: Create docs/security/pentestagent/findings/ledger.md — a master table of all findings from all playbooks. Columns: ID, Category, Severity, Affected Endpoint/File, Description, Playbook, Status (open/fixed/wontfix), Fix Commit, Re-verified At.

stories.title: Fix high-severity findings
stories.details: For each high-severity finding: create a fix commit, update the ledger, re-run the relevant playbook, document re-verification. Possible high-severity areas: XSS in chat input, SSRF in chat endpoint, auth bypass in webhook, missing rate limiting, missing security headers.

stories.title: Fix medium-severity findings
stories.details: For each medium-severity finding: create a fix commit, update the ledger, re-run the relevant playbook, document re-verification. Possible medium-severity areas: CSP improvements, CORS hardening, cookie flags, dependency vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Fix low-severity and informational findings
stories.details: For each low-severity/informational finding: create a fix commit, update the ledger, re-run the relevant playbook, document re-verification. Possible low-severity areas: verbose error messages, missing security.txt, missing .well-known/ paths, documentation gaps.

stories.title: Wontfix and accepted-risk documentation
stories.details: For findings marked as wontfix or accepted risk: document the rationale, any compensating controls, and the acceptance authority. Examples: unsafe-inline CSP for dev mode, Cal.com iframe sandbox limitations.

stories.title: Full re-scan after all remediations
stories.details: Run the full PentestAgent playbook suite after all remediations. Capture the final scan results. Update the ledger with final status. Generate the remediation summary report.

epics.title: Security documentation & dashboard
epics.summary: Create the comprehensive security documentation: security dashboard, posture score, security.txt, security policy, agent skill, and README badges. This is the showcase layer that demonstrates the security engineering work.

stories.title: Create security dashboard
stories.details: Write docs/security/dashboard.md — a visual dashboard showing: overall posture score, per-category scores (recon, vuln scan, API security, infrastructure), finding counts by severity, fix rate, last scan date, CI pipeline status. Use ASCII tables and status badges.

stories.title: Create security posture score model
stories.details: Write docs/security/posture-score.md — define the scoring model: 10 categories × 10 points each = 100 max. Categories: API security, headers, CSP, cookies/TLS, recon coverage, vuln coverage, input validation, auth, dependencies, CI integration. Each category has pass/fail criteria.

stories.title: Deploy security.txt and .well-known/
stories.details: Create public/.well-known/security.txt with the security policy, contact info, disclosure policy, and PGP key. Create public/.well-known/ directory placeholder. Wire into Next.js static serving if needed.

stories.title: Author .agents/skills/run-pentestagent/SKILL.md
stories.details: Write the agent skill for running PentestAgent: prerequisites, env setup, playbook execution, reading findings, remediation workflow, CI integration. Include copy-pasteable command templates for each playbook.

stories.title: Update README with security badges
stories.details: Add security posture badge, PentestAgent badge, and last scan date to README.md. Add a Security section with links to dashboard and security.txt.

epics.title: Final verification & showcase PR
epics.summary: Final verification run of all playbooks, generation of the final comprehensive security report, and creation of the showcase PR from security/pentestagent into main.

stories.title: Run full PentestAgent suite final pass
stories.details: Run every playbook in sequence: recon → fingerprint → endpoint extraction → dir enum → subdomain → XSS → CSRF → SSRF → injection → misconfig → data exposure → rate limit → auth bypass → input validation → CORS → fuzz → dependency → headers → CSP → cookies → TLS → cloud. Capture all results.

stories.title: Generate comprehensive security report
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/reports/comprehensive-security-report.md — the final report covering: executive summary, methodology, scope, findings summary, detailed findings, remediation summary, residual risk, posture score, recommendations, appendices (playbook list, tool versions, timeline).

stories.title: Open showcase PR
stories.details: Create the PR from security/pentestagent into main with title 'sec(pentestagent): integrate PentestAgent AI security testing framework — top-tier security posture'. The PR body documents the full journey: 8 epics, 40+ stories, all playbooks, all findings, all remediations, CI integration, and the security dashboard.

stories.title: Create PR notes for security showcase
stories.details: Write docs/security/pentestagent/PR_NOTES.md — the full PR description with: narrative, score table, epic summaries, commit map, verification results, reviewer guide, and security engineer portfolio talking points.
